full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Quddus, J:- This Rule Nisi, was issued at the instance of the writ petitioner Md. Arif Gaffer, a judgment debtor in an exparte decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna to examine the legality of order dated 1.12.2008 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna issuing warrant of arrest for his civil imprisonment in Artha Jari Case No. 185 of 2006 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 27 of 2006). 

 2. The facts leading to the present writ petition are that Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd. and its Khulna Branch as plaintiffs (herein respondent Nos.2-3) instituted Artha Rin Suit No.27 of 2006 before the Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna against Makkah Poultry Feeds Ltd. a registered company and its directors for realisation of loan amounting Tk. 1,78,54,736/- (one crore seventy eight lac fifty four thousand seven hundred thirty six only). The writ petitioner being Managing Director of the said company was made defendant No.2 in the suit. Ultimately the suit was decreed exparte by judgment and decree dated 20.4.2006 for realisation of the said amount. The decree-holder hank put the decree in execution by filing Artha Jari Case No. 185 of 2006. In course of the execution proceedings; the decree holder bank unsuccessfully attempted to sell the property given as collateral against the loan. At one stage there was a negotiation between the parties, following which the writ petitioner paid Tk, 32,00,000/. (Thirty two lac only) to the bank and was awaiting settlement of the dispute in a friendly manner. Surprisingly the bank discontinued the negotiation and filed an application on 1.12.2008 before the executing Court for issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioner in order to put him in civil prison upon which the executing Court issued warrant of arrest against him by its order dated 1.12.2008 without any show cause notice as-required under Order XXI rule 37 of the Code of Civil Procedure and forwarded the same to the concerned police station in a hasty manner. On the, following day i.e, on 2.12.2008 the police arrested the petitioner and sent him to prison. Being aggrieved by the said order, the petitioner moved the present writ petition, obtained a Rule and ad-interim order of bail, which was extended from time to time. 

 3. The. Khulna Branch of Islamic Bank Bangladesh Ltd. (respondent No.3) contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter-alia, that after commencement of the execution proceedings the decree holder bank issued notice under section 30 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 and it was returned to the executing Court after proper service upon the judgment debtors. The writ petitioner appeared before the executing Court on 14.9.2006 and filed application praying for, stay of the execution proceedings on the ground of filing Writ Petition NO.8316 of 2006 before the High Court Division. Subsequently he obtained a Rule and Order of stay from the High Court Division in the said writ petition on 17.9.2006. However, the Hon'ble Court ultimately discharged the Rule vacating the said order of stay. The decree holder bank also published auction notice in news-papers and wanted to sell the mortgaged property, but failed. Thereafter the bank, in order to compel the judgment debtor for payment of the decretal amount, filed application of warrant of arrest to put him in civil prison under sections 34 and 35 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The executing Court allowed the said application and issued .warrant of arrest against him on 1.12.2008 and fixed 5.1 009 for compliance of the warrant, as the bank had no other way but to move for his (petitioner's) civil imprisonment. 

 "27. From a combined reading of those sub-sections of section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 it manifests, that the Adalat is empowered to pass an order of warrant of arrest/ civil imprisonment' directly on the basis of an application filed by the decree-holder bank when no auction sale is possible to be held for any reason. 

 The same view was upheld in 14 BLC, 107, although the Rule was made absolute in that case on the ground that the application for civil imprisonment was not filed by the decree-holder bank, as per provision of the law. 

 9. The requirement of natural justice depends on the facts and circumstance of a case, the nature of inquiry, the rules under which the Court or Tribunal is acting, the subject matter that is being dealt with and many other aspects. In the present case the petitioner being a defaulter. loanee was sued upon under a special law and after service of summons the suit was decreed exparte against him. On subsequent commencement of the execution proceedings, a notice under section, 30 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain was also served upon him and an attempt was made to sell the property that was given as collateral against the loan. Under the circumstance, the writ petitioner was supposed to know the legal consequence of the execution proceedings. In such a case no more notice to show cause was necessary before issuance of warrant of arrest against him, for compliance of natural justice.
